name: jevlint-le-mcp

tools.name: lint_text
tools.description: Lint questions written for a decision model before they are sent: TypeSafe's Jev (System One, /v1/systemone) and OpenAI's Decisions API (gpt-6-luna, /v1/decisions), in either request shape, or the Vercel AI SDK's decide() for both. Pass a request body as JSON, or source code that builds one. Returns each finding with its rule, message, position and docs link, the edit that would mend it when there is one, plus how many questions were found and how many could not be read in full. Use it after writing or changing a question. It sends nothing over the network.

text.description: The request JSON or the source code.

filename.description: A file name whose extension says what the text is: .json, .ts, .js, .py, .rs or .go. Defaults to request.jev.json.

rules.description: Rule levels to override, such as { "DEC004": "off" }. Levels: off, hint, info, warning, error.

tools.name: lint_paths
tools.description: Lint the Jev and OpenAI Decisions questions in files or directories on disk. A directory is searched for the file types the linter reads. Returns the same report as lint_text, one entry per file. It sends nothing over the network.

paths.description: Files or directories on disk, relative to the directory the server was started in.

rules.description: Rule levels to override, such as { "DEC004": "off" }. Levels: off, hint, info, warning, error.

tools.name: fix_text
tools.description: Apply the safe fixes to a request body or source code passed as text, and return the mended text with how many findings were mended and the report of what is left. A safe fix only mends what the API would refuse: a criteria key written yes where it takes true, a mistyped question type, criteria in the wrong shape. A fix that changes what a working request does, such as adding a fallback option or pinning a model, is never applied here. It stays in the report with its edit marked safe: false, for you to make or to leave. Nothing is written to disk and nothing is sent over the network.

text.description: The request JSON or the source code.

filename.description: A file name whose extension says what the text is: .json, .ts, .js, .py, .rs or .go. Defaults to request.jev.json.

rules.description: Rule levels to override, such as { "DEC004": "off" }. Levels: off, hint, info, warning, error.

tools.name: list_rules
tools.description: List every rule with its code, name, what it catches, default level, its own page with an example, the vendor page behind it, and whether it runs offline here or only when ask_model asks the model.

tools.name: explain_rule
tools.description: A rule's own page, as Markdown: what it catches, an example that is flagged with the message the linter gives, one that is not, how to fix it and how to silence it. Use it before making a fix that fix_text leaves to you, or before silencing a finding.

tools.name: plan_ask
tools.description: Say what ask_model would send for the given text or paths, and send nothing: how many requests, to which model, about how many input tokens, how many questions are held back for having a part built at runtime, and how many fall past maxCalls. Needs no key. Call it first when the user wants to know the cost of a check before paying for it.

text.description: The request JSON or the source code.

filename.description: A file name whose extension says what the text is: .json, .ts, .js, .py, .rs or .go. Defaults to request.jev.json.

paths.description: Files or directories on disk, relative to the directory the server was started in.

rules.description: Rule levels to override, such as { "DEC004": "off" }. Levels: off, hint, info, warning, error.

platform.description: Where to send, named outright: typesafe for Jev, openai for Luna, or openrouter, vercel, llmgateway or liquid. Each has its own key variable and a default model. Without it the model id goes where its spelling says, or to DECISIONLINT_ASK_ENDPOINT.

model.description: The model to ask: a Jev version, gpt-6-luna for OpenAI's Decisions API, or a model id in another platform's spelling, such as ~typesafe/jev-latest for OpenRouter. It is sent to the platform the spelling names, or to DECISIONLINT_ASK_ENDPOINT in the environment the server was started with, which is never an argument. Defaults to jev-1.13.0, which the checks were measured on.

maxCalls.description: The most requests the call may send. Defaults to 25. Requests past it are counted and not sent.

sendState.description: Also send the state written out in the text, to the checks that read it. Defaults to false.

tools.name: ask_model
tools.description: Ask the model itself, TypeSafe's Jev or OpenAI's Luna, to check the questions in the given text or paths after linting them: overlapping options, a question that needs counting, a label that does not match its description, and the other checks list_rules marks runsHere: false. This sends the questions to the vendor with the user's own API key and costs money, so call it only when the user asks for a check with Jev or Luna, never on every edit, and use plan_ask first when the cost matters. The key is read from the platform's own variable, TYPESAFE_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, LLM_GATEWAY_API_KEY or LIQUID_API_KEY, in the environment the server was started with, or from .env.local or .env in its working directory, and is never taken as an argument. Where the requests go is the platform the model id's spelling names, or DECISIONLINT_ASK_ENDPOINT in that environment for a host the user runs, never an argument either. Returns the lint report with the model's findings added, each with the probability the model gave, what was sent and answered, and why the check fell short when it did. Bounded by maxCalls.

tools.name: probe_question
tools.description: Send one question to Jev several times, as written and with its layout changed, options reversed, labels hidden, levels reversed, criteria removed, to see whether the answer holds. Returns a report as Markdown with a verdict and which variants moved the decision. The text must carry the state the question is asked against, and when it has more than one question, questionId names the one. Asks Jev only, about a dozen requests, with the user's TypeSafe key found the way ask_model finds it. It costs money, so call it only when the user asks to probe a question.

text.description: The request JSON or the source code.

filename.description: A file name whose extension says what the text is: .json, .ts, .js, .py, .rs or .go. Defaults to request.jev.json.

questionId.description: The id of the question to probe. Needed when the text has more than one.

model.description: A Jev version. Defaults to jev-1.13.0.

instructions: Lints questions written for a decision model, TypeSafe's Jev or OpenAI's Decisions API (gpt-6-luna), before they are sent. Call lint_text after writing or changing a question, in a request body or in code. Call fix_text for the mended text where the fix is certain, and explain_rule for a rule's page with an example before making the fixes it leaves to you. Those, lint_paths, list_rules and plan_ask send nothing and need no key. ask_model and probe_question send the questions to the vendor with the user's own API key and cost money: call them only when the user asks for a check with Jev or Luna, or for a probe. The server writes nothing.
